subject: cult-info-fo
title: CULT.INFO.FO.------POL.DY.
description: Diagram in EXT.F(II)-15. (C)CULT-INFO-F (the concept of culture information focus) is crossed with POL-DYM (political dynamics). MPT (manipulation, the reality of) → CULT-INFO-F; AFL (affinity alignment) → CULT-INFO-F. CULT-INFO-F → EXT-FT (extended functionalism) → PART (participation) → POL-P (political policies). A separate sub-chain: POL-DYM (the crossing) → SOC-RT (social reality) → (R)INTR (real interpretation). MT-INFO (music information) → INTR. P-PROG (particular progressionalism) → AFL. Structural argument: the *concept* of culture information focus is fed by manipulation and by affinity alignment — meaning culture information focus is structurally constituted by both the manipulation-apparatus and the underlying affinity. The productive output runs through extended functionalism into participation into political policies — meaning culture information focus's main downstream chain *terminates* at political policies. The political-dynamics → social-reality → real-interpretation chain runs in parallel, with music information feeding interpretation as a parallel input. The diagram thus diagrams a sharp diagnostic: when culture information focus is conceptually grasped (the (c) prefix), its productive line ends at political policies — and political dynamics' separate chain to real interpretation runs alongside, with music information also reaching interpretation. Real interpretation and political policies are *separate* terminal outputs, not converging — meaning Braxton's structural claim is that the political-policies layer and the real-interpretation layer remain divergent in the seventies despite all the cross-continental work and integration efforts.
